entry.title: The Agent Contract Problem: When Your Agent Commits to Something It Can't Deliver
entry.summary:
The Agent Contract Problem: When Your Agent Commits to Something It Can't Deliver
Every autonomous agent will eventually make a promise it can't keep. Not through malice — through the gap between what the agent understood when it agreed and what the task actually required when execution began. This is the agent contract problem, and it's the silent killer of agent reliability. When you delegate a task to an agent, you're making an implicit contract. The agent says "I'll handle it" — often with more confidence than it should. The agent processes your request, estimates its capability to fulfill it, and commits to the task before it has full visibility into what's actually involved. This isn't unique to AI. Human contractors face the same problem. A contractor who bids low to win the job, …

entry.title: Review Latency Is a Visibility Problem, Not a People Problem
entry.summary:
The Real Bottleneck in Your Development Cycle
Most engineering teams think they have a review speed problem. They set SLA targets, schedule dedicated review blocks, and nag people in Slack. But after looking at patterns across many teams this week, one thing became very clear: the bottleneck is rarely how fast someone reviews a PR. Introducing Blazar: Quicknode's Purpose-Built Solana WebSocket Solution
entry.summary: Solana's native WebSocket PubSub drops messages under load and leaves three subscription methods unstable. Blazar fixes that at the infrastructure level, with sub-millisecond overhead, full method support, and no SDK changes required.
